tasks.title: Check Website Page Speed & Mobile Loading
tasks.goal: Pages load in under 3 seconds on mobile phones
steps: Test your top 5 most visited pages on a mobile phone
Compress large photos so they load quickly without losing quality
Make sure buttons and text are easy to read without zooming in

tasks.title: Write Clear Page Titles & Search Descriptions
tasks.goal: Get more people to click your website link on Google
steps: Include the main topic phrase naturally in your page title (under 60 characters)
Write a clear 1-2 sentence summary (under 155 characters) explaining how the page helps
Make sure every page on your site has its own unique title

tasks.title: Fix Broken Website Links (404 Pages)
tasks.goal: Zero dead links that frustrate visitors
tasks.tools: Google Search Console, Broken Link Checker
steps: Check for any links that lead to a 'Page Not Found' screen
Update old links so they point to the right live page
Add helpful links between related blog posts and product pages

tasks.title: Update Google Business Profile for Local Customers
tasks.goal: Rank in the top 3 local results on Google Maps
steps: Confirm your business hours, phone number, and address are accurate
Upload 2-3 fresh photos of your products, team, or store
Reply warmly to every new customer review within 24 hours

tasks.title: Research Questions Customers Are Searching For
tasks.goal: Create 4 new helpful blog articles or FAQ guides each month
tasks.tools: Google Search 'People Also Ask', Google Trends, AnswerThePublic
steps: List the top 10 questions customers ask before buying your product
Look up those questions on Google to see what pages currently show up
Write a clearer, more helpful answer with step-by-step examples

tasks.title: Review Daily Ad Spend & Pause Non-Performing Ads
tasks.goal: Keep ad spending on budget and stop wasting money on weak ads
tasks.tools: Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads
steps: Check how much money was spent yesterday vs your daily budget target
Pause any ad that has spent 2x your target cost per sale without getting results
Move budget toward the ads bringing in the most sales or leads

tasks.title: Remove Irrelevant Search Words from Google Ads
tasks.goal: Save 15%+ of your ad budget by blocking wrong searches
steps: Open the list of actual words people typed before clicking your ad
Add unrelated words (like 'free', 'jobs', or 'cheap DIY') to your block list
Put your best-performing search phrases into their own focused ad group

tasks.title: Refresh Ad Videos & Headlines When People Get Tired of Them
tasks.goal: Keep click rates above 1.5% on social media ads
steps: Check if the same audience has seen your ad more than 3-4 times
Create 3 new opening hooks (the first 3 seconds of your video)
Test a customer testimonial photo against a clean product demonstration

tasks.title: Set Up Follow-Up Ads (Retargeting) for Window Shoppers
tasks.goal: Bring back visitors who viewed a product or cart but didn't buy
tasks.tools: Meta Ads, Google Ads Audience Manager
steps: Show a helpful reminder ad to people who visited in the last 14 days
Exclude people who already bought so you don't waste money showing them the same ad
Include customer reviews or a small first-order bonus to answer doubts

tasks.title: Film & Edit Short Vertical Videos (Reels, TikTok & Shorts)
tasks.goal: Keep viewers watching past the first 3 seconds
tasks.tools: CapCut, Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts
steps: Start with a strong question or visual result in the very first 2 seconds
Add clear on-screen captions so people can watch with their sound off
End with one simple instruction (e.g., 'Comment GUIDE' or 'Tap link in bio')

tasks.title: Turn One Big Topic into a Full Week of Social Posts
tasks.goal: Publish consistently across 3-4 platforms without burnout
steps: Take 1 helpful guide or customer story as your main weekly theme
Turn the key points into a 5-slide swipeable carousel post
Record a 30-second talking-head video summarizing the #1 takeaway

tasks.title: Reply to Comments, Direct Messages & Brand Mentions
tasks.goal: Reply to potential customers within 1 hour during work hours
steps: Answer questions on your posts and Ads with friendly, helpful replies
Send direct links to people who asked about pricing or availability in DMs
Write down common customer questions to use as future post ideas

tasks.title: Check Automated Welcome & Abandoned Cart Emails
tasks.goal: Convert new email signups and recover unfinished shopping carts
steps: Sign up with a test email to make sure the Welcome Email arrives immediately
Check that all buttons and discount codes inside the email work on mobile
Test two different subject lines to see which one gets more opens

tasks.title: Send Weekly Value Newsletter to Email Subscribers
tasks.goal: Achieve 30%+ open rate and steady clicks to your website
steps: Share 1 useful tip or story alongside 1 clear product or service offer
Keep paragraphs short (1-2 sentences) with a single clear call-to-action button
Preview the email in both Light Mode and Dark Mode before sending

tasks.title: Clean Out Inactive Email Addresses to Protect Deliverability
tasks.goal: Keep your emails landing in the main Inbox instead of the Spam folder
steps: Find subscribers who haven't opened a single email in the last 90 days
Send one short 'Still want to hear from us?' check-in email
Remove addresses that bounce or never respond so email providers trust your sender name

tasks.title: Simplify Your Landing Page & Checkout Steps
tasks.goal: Increase the percentage of visitors who buy or sign up
steps: Make sure the main headline clearly states what you offer and who it helps
Place customer reviews and star ratings near the 'Buy' or 'Book Now' button
Remove unnecessary form fields so customers can check out in under 60 seconds

tasks.title: Add Tracking Links (UTM Tags) to Every Campaign Link
tasks.goal: Know exactly which post, email, or ad brought in each sale
steps: Tag every shared link with its source (e.g., instagram, newsletter, google_ads)
Test the link on your phone to make sure it opens the right page quickly
Keep a simple list of your campaign links so your team uses consistent names

tasks.title: Review Weekly Marketing Results & Best-Performing Channels
tasks.goal: Double down on what works and stop doing what doesn't
steps: Compare total marketing money spent against total sales revenue earned
Identify the #1 social post, #1 email, and #1 ad from the past 7 days
Write down 3 clear action steps for next week's marketing plan

contentPlanner.title: Weekly Performance Review & Ad Budget Check
contentPlanner.notes: Review last week's total sales, check Cost Per Lead in the Calculator tab, and shift budget to your top-performing ads.

contentPlanner.title: Publish 1 Helpful Guide or Answer a Customer FAQ
contentPlanner.notes: Write a clear article answering a common customer question and share a short summary on your Google Business Profile.

contentPlanner.title: Post Educational Reel / TikTok / YouTube Short
contentPlanner.notes: Hook viewers in the first 3 seconds, demonstrate how your product solves a problem, and invite viewers to click the link in your bio.

contentPlanner.title: Send Weekly Value Newsletter & Promotional Offer
contentPlanner.notes: Write a curiosity-driven subject line, keep paragraphs brief for mobile readers, and include one bold button linking to your offer.

contentPlanner.title: Share Customer Review Carousel & Reply to All DMs
contentPlanner.notes: Highlight real customer results, follow up with anyone who asked questions in your comments or messages this week, and schedule weekend posts.

contentPlanner.title: New Promo Launch Checklist & Retargeting Setup
contentPlanner.notes: Double-check all checkout buttons on mobile, test promo codes, turn on retargeting ads for window shoppers, and calculate target ROAS.

glossary.simple: How many dollars (or pesos) you earn back for every $1 or ₱1 you spend on ads.
glossary.formula: ROAS = Revenue from Ads ÷ Ad Spend
glossary.example: If you spend ₱5,000 on Facebook Ads and get ₱20,000 in sales, your ROAS is 4.0x (you earned 4 times what you spent).

glossary.simple: Your actual net profit percentage after subtracting both your product costs and marketing costs.
glossary.formula: ROI (%) = ((Net Profit ÷ Total Cost) × 100)
glossary.example: If a campaign costs ₱10,000 total and brings in ₱15,000 in profit after product costs, your ROI is +50%.

glossary.simple: The average amount you pay each time someone clicks on your ad.
glossary.formula: CPC = Total Ad Spend ÷ Total Clicks
glossary.example: Spending ₱1,000 on an ad that gets 200 clicks means your Cost Per Click is ₱5.00.

glossary.simple: Out of every 100 people who see your ad, email, or link, how many actually click it.
glossary.formula: CTR (%) = (Total Clicks ÷ Total Views) × 100
glossary.example: If 1,000 people see your post and 25 click your link, your CTR is 2.5%.

glossary.simple: How much marketing money it costs you to win 1 paying customer.
glossary.formula: CPA = Total Ad Spend ÷ Number of New Customers
glossary.example: If you spend ₱3,000 on ads and get 10 buyers, your Cost Per Customer is ₱300.

glossary.simple: How much you pay to get 1 interested person's contact info (like their email or phone number).
glossary.formula: CPL = Total Ad Spend ÷ Total Leads Collected
glossary.example: Spending ₱2,000 to get 40 people to sign up for a free quote gives you a ₱50 Cost Per Lead.

glossary.simple: The price an ad platform charges to show your ad 1,000 times.
glossary.formula: CPM = (Ad Spend ÷ Impressions) × 1,000
glossary.example: If you spend ₱500 and your ad is shown 10,000 times, your CPM is ₱50.

glossary.simple: The percentage of website visitors who take action (buy a product, book a call, or sign up).
glossary.formula: Conversion Rate (%) = (Conversions ÷ Total Visitors) × 100
glossary.example: If 500 people visit your product page and 15 buy, your Conversion Rate is 3.0%.

glossary.simple: A focused web page designed for one specific goal — such as getting a visitor to buy one product or sign up for a free guide.
glossary.formula: 1 Clear Headline + Benefits + Social Proof + 1 Action Button
glossary.example: Sending ad clicks to a dedicated offer page instead of a busy homepage usually doubles your sales.

glossary.simple: The specific button or instruction telling people what step to take next.
glossary.formula: Action Verb + Clear Benefit
glossary.example: 'Get My Free Price Quote', 'Shop the Summer Sale', or 'Comment GUIDE below'.

glossary.simple: The average amount a customer spends each time they place an order with you.
glossary.formula: AOV = Total Revenue ÷ Total Orders
glossary.example: If 10 orders bring in ₱12,000 total, your Average Order Value is ₱1,200.

glossary.simple: The total amount of money a typical customer spends with your business over the entire time they buy from you.
glossary.formula: LTV = Average Order Value × Repeat Purchases Per Year × Years
glossary.example: A coffee shop customer who spends ₱200 twice a week is worth over ₱20,000 per year.

glossary.simple: Improving your website so it shows up higher for free when people search on Google.
glossary.formula: Helpful Content + Fast Mobile Site + Clear Keywords
glossary.example: Writing a detailed page titled 'Best Wedding Photographer in Manila' so couples find you on Google without paid ads.

glossary.simple: The exact words and questions people type into Google, YouTube, or TikTok when looking for something.
glossary.formula: Topic + Customer Intent (e.g., 'buy', 'best', 'how to')
glossary.example: 'Affordable dental clinic Pasig' is a high-intent keyword because the searcher is ready to book.

glossary.simple: Organic traffic comes to your site naturally for free (from search or regular posts); Paid traffic comes from ads you pay for.
glossary.formula: Total Traffic = Organic Visitors + Paid Ad Visitors
glossary.example: A viral TikTok video brings free organic traffic; a boosted Facebook post brings paid traffic.

glossary.simple: Showing follow-up ads to warm prospects who already visited your website or watched your videos.
glossary.formula: Past Visitors → Reminder Ad → Completed Purchase
glossary.example: When you look at a pair of shoes online and see an ad for those exact shoes on Instagram 10 minutes later.

glossary.simple: The journey a stranger takes from first discovering your brand to becoming a loyal paying customer.
glossary.formula: 1. Awareness (Discover) → 2. Consideration (Trust) → 3. Conversion (Buy)
glossary.example: Someone watches your helpful Reel (Awareness), downloads your price guide (Consideration), and books a package (Conversion).

glossary.simple: A free, useful resource you give away in exchange for a visitor's email address or phone number.
glossary.formula: Free Checklist / Discount / Sample = New Email Subscriber
glossary.example: 'Enter your email to get 10% off your first order' or 'Download our free 7-day meal planner'.

glossary.simple: Open Rate is the % of subscribers who open your email; Click Rate is the % who tap a link inside it.
glossary.formula: Open Rate = (Opens ÷ Delivered) × 100
glossary.example: Out of 1,000 subscribers, 350 open the email (35% Open Rate) and 40 click the product link (4% Click Rate).

glossary.simple: How actively people interact with your post through likes, comments, shares, and saves.
glossary.formula: Engagement Rate (%) = ((Likes + Comments + Shares + Saves) ÷ Reach) × 100
glossary.example: A post seen by 1,000 people that gets 60 likes, comments, and saves has a strong 6.0% Engagement Rate.

glossary.simple: Showing two versions of an ad, email subject line, or page (Version A vs. Version B) to see which one performs better.
glossary.formula: Change 1 Thing at a Time → Measure Winner
glossary.example: Testing a red 'Buy Now' button against a green 'Claim Offer' button to see which gets more clicks.

glossary.simple: Small labels added to the end of a web link so Google Analytics can tell you exactly which post or ad brought the visitor.
glossary.formula: website.com/?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=bio
glossary.example: Helps you prove whether your sales came from your Instagram bio link, your Thursday email, or your Facebook ad.

glossary.simple: The percentage of visitors who open your page and leave right away without clicking anything or taking action.
glossary.formula: Single-Page Exits ÷ Total Visits × 100
glossary.example: If a page takes 10 seconds to load or looks confusing on mobile, visitors leave immediately (high bounce rate).

glossary.simple: Authentic photos, unboxing videos, or reviews filmed by real customers or creators rather than polished studio commercials.
glossary.formula: Real Person + Honest Product Demo = High Trust
glossary.example: A smartphone video of a happy customer showing how they use your skincare routine at home.
